subject: EFA and CFA on the same set of data

messages.author: 8ca021d088ca9d62
messages.subject: EFA and CFA on the same set of data
parts:
Hi all

I'm using lavaal for exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis for a set of dichotomous items. The problem is that i'm dealing with longitudinal data and my sample size is too small (only 66 companies for each time point)

the problem is that I want to confirm the results of the EFA by a confirmatory analysis but I can't split the sample because it becomes too small (33 companies). Is it justifiable to run these two analyses on the same set of data in such cases?

THANKS a lot for your help

Rania

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: EFA and CFA on the same set of data
parts:
Hi

No, is not justifiable to run and EFA and CFA on the same data. It becomes redundant results, the CFA is constraint version of the EFA. With the same sample it may lead to a false sense of confidence, the CFA will always agree with the EFA

I dont recommend using EFA very often, from my point if you decide to use EFA from the beginning has to be because there is NO information about the structural form of the items, this is not cases in most circumstances.

Also, If I remember properly the sample size requirements for EFA are quiet high, specially with categorical indicators (remember to use a proper estimator). Since CFA is a constraint version of the EFA it requires less sample.

Good luck
